hausman

Hausman comparison of fixed and random effects

Stata 

hausman fixed random

R plm 

plm::phtest(fe, re)

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Requires same regressors and compatible covariance assumptions.

Stata reference · R reference

xtcloglog

Random-intercept panel cloglog

Stata 

xtcloglog binary x, re

R lme4 

lme4::glmer(binary ~ x + (1 | id), data = data, family = stats::binomial(link = "cloglog"), nAGQ = 12)

Differs from Stata Uses normal panel random intercepts and 12-point adaptive quadrature, matching Stata intpoints(12). Quadrature adaptation and convergence criteria remain package-specific.

Stata reference · R reference

xtgee

binomial GEE with exchangeable working correlation

Stata 

xtgee binary x, family( binomial ) corr( exchangeable ) vce(robust)

R geepack 

geepack::geeglm(binary ~ x, id = id, waves = time, data = data, family = stats::binomial(), corstr = "exchangeable")

Differs from Stata Rows must be sorted into contiguous id panels with correctly ordered waves. The displayed vce(robust) explicitly matches geeglm sandwich standard errors; family, link and working correlation are specified. Numerical correlation/scale iteration tolerances may differ.

Stata reference · R reference

Differs from Stata Rows must be sorted into contiguous id panels with correctly ordered waves. The displayed vce(robust) explicitly matches geeglm sandwich standard errors; family, link and working correlation are specified. Numerical correlation/scale iteration tolerances may differ.

xtgls

Group-heteroskedastic panel GLS by maximum likelihood

Stata 

xtgls y x z, panels(heteroskedastic) igls

R nlme 

nlme::gls(y ~ x + z, data = data, weights = nlme::varIdent(form = ~1 | id), method = "ML")

Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Common slopes with independent residuals and group-specific residual variances; likelihood, variance normalization and convergence criteria can differ.

Stata reference · R reference

xthtaylor

Hausman-Taylor model with time-varying and invariant endogenous covariates

Stata 

xthtaylor y x1 x2 a b, endog(x2 b) constant(a b)

R plm 

plm::plm(y ~ x1 + x2 + a + b | x1 + a | x2, data = data, index = c("id", "time"), random.method = "ht", model = "random", inst.method = "baltagi")

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. The three-part R formula explicitly separates exogenous covariates and time-varying endogenous covariates. Identification of invariant endogenous effects requires sufficient exogenous time-varying instruments; these classifications need substantive justification.

Stata reference · R reference

xtivreg

Fixed-effects instrumental-variable regression

Stata 

xtivreg y z (x = instrument), fe

R plm 

plm::plm(y ~ x + z | instrument + z, data = pd, model = "within")

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Instrument validity must be justified substantively; this fixture only verifies execution.

Stata reference · R reference

xtlogit

Conditional fixed-effects logistic regression

Stata 

xtlogit binary x, fe

R survival 

{ coxph <- survival::coxph; survival::clogit(binary ~ x + survival::strata(id), data = data) }

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Conditions out group intercepts; groups without outcome variation contribute no coefficient information.

Stata reference · R reference

xtpcse

Beck-Katz panel-corrected covariance

Stata 

xtpcse y x z, correlation(independent)

R plm 

{ fit <- plm::plm(y ~ x + z, data = pd, model = "pooling"); lmtest::coeftest(fit, vcov. = plm::vcovBK(fit, type = "HC0", cluster = "time"), df = Inf) }

Differs from Stata Pooled OLS with Beck-Katz contemporaneous cross-panel covariance. pd must be balanced and complete with identical time order. HC0 and df=Inf give the unadjusted PCSE and normal-reference coefficient tests.

Stata reference · R reference

xtpoisson

Random-intercept panel Poisson

Stata 

xtpoisson count x, re normal

R lme4 

lme4::glmer(count ~ x + (1 | id), data = data, family = stats::poisson(link = "log"), nAGQ = 12)

Differs from Stata Uses normal panel random intercepts and 12-point adaptive quadrature, matching the Stata integration-point default. xtpoisson requires re normal for this distribution; its plain re default is gamma. Quadrature adaptation and convergence criteria remain package-specific.

Stata 

xtreg y x z i.time, fe

Stata reference · R reference

Random-effects panel regression

Stata 

xtreg y x z, re sa

R plm 

plm::plm(y ~ x + z, data = pd, model = "random", effect = "individual")

Differs from Stata Stata sa and R random.method="swar" both select Swamy-Arora variance components. pd must declare the same id and time indexes. This is the sa specification, not Stata default re.

Stata reference · R reference

4 more examples and alternatives

Fit a within-panel fixed-effects regression

Stata 

xtreg y x z, fe

R plm 

plm::plm(y ~ x + z, data = pd, model = "within", effect = "individual")

Both commands fit individual fixed effects using the within transformation. plm reports the transformed-model coefficient vector without Stata reported intercept; residual degrees of freedom and covariance scaling must be aligned separately.

Stata reference · R reference

Cluster-robust panel standard errors

Stata 

xtreg y x z, fe vce(cluster id)

R plm 

{ V <- plm::vcovHC(fit, method = "arellano", type = "sss", cluster = "group"); G <- length(unique(plm::index(fit)[[1L]])); lmtest::coeftest(fit, vcov. = V, df = G - 1L) }

Differs from Stata fit is the matching individual within model. type="sss" uses Stata cluster finite-sample scaling; the t reference uses the number of panels minus one. Require independent clusters and identical estimation samples.

Stata reference · R reference

Cluster-robust within-panel standard errors

Stata 

xtreg y x z, fe vce(robust)

R plm 

{ V <- plm::vcovHC(fit, method = "arellano", type = "sss", cluster = "group"); G <- length(unique(plm::index(fit)[[1L]])); lmtest::coeftest(fit, vcov. = V, df = G - 1L) }

Differs from Stata fit is the matching individual within model. type="sss" uses Stata cluster finite-sample scaling; the t reference uses the number of panels minus one. Require independent clusters and identical estimation samples.

Stata reference · R reference

Random effects with swar variance components

Stata 

xtreg y x z, re sa

R plm 

plm::plm(y ~ x + z, data = pd, model = "random", random.method = "swar")

Stata sa and R random.method="swar" both select Swamy-Arora variance components. pd must declare the same id and time indexes. This is the sa specification, not Stata default re.

Stata reference · R reference

xtscc

Driscoll-Kraay covariance

Stata 

xtscc y x z, fe lag(2)

R plm 

{ full <- plm::within_intercept(fit, return.model = TRUE); V <- plm::vcovSCC(full, type = "sss", maxlag = 2); lmtest::coeftest(full, vcov. = V)[c("x", "z"), , drop = FALSE] }

Differs from Stata Community command xtscc uses a within transformation with the grand mean restored. within_intercept reconstructs that fitted model; sss selects Stata-type small-sample scaling and maxlag=2 fixes the Bartlett bandwidth. Reported reference degrees of freedom can differ by implementation/version.

Stata reference · R reference

xtunitroot

Panel unit-root test: madwu

Stata 

xtunitroot fisher y, dfuller lags(1)

R plm 

plm::purtest(pd$y, test = "madwu", exo = "intercept", lags = 1, pmax = 1)

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Hadri reverses the null to stationarity; deterministic terms and lag rules must match.

Stata reference · R reference

Panel unit-root test: hadri

Stata 

xtunitroot hadri y, robust

R plm 

plm::purtest(pd$y, test = "hadri", exo = "intercept", Hcons = TRUE)

Differs from Stata The null is panel stationarity. Hcons=TRUE selects the heteroskedasticity-robust Hadri statistic, corresponding to Stata robust; plm ignores lag selections for Hadri and provides no Bartlett HAC kernel correction.

Stata reference · R reference

Panel unit-root test: ips

Stata 

xtunitroot ips y, lags(1)

R plm 

plm::purtest(pd$y, test = "ips", exo = "intercept", lags = 1, pmax = 1)

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Hadri reverses the null to stationarity; deterministic terms and lag rules must match.

Stata reference · R reference

Panel unit-root test: levinlin

Stata 

xtunitroot llc y, lags(1)

R plm 

plm::purtest(pd$y, test = "levinlin", exo = "intercept", lags = 1, pmax = 1, q = floor(3.21 * max(table(plm::index(pd)[[1L]]))^(1/3)))

Differs from Stata Complete balanced panel with an intercept and one ADF lag. The explicit Bartlett bandwidth floor(3.21*T^(1/3)) matches Stata default LLC truncation; no cross-sectional demeaning is applied.
